assessments.reasoning: At [336,540) the official annotated tag object records v3.29.0 and a commit target of 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. This matches the raw UK v2.0 detail revision. The tag object’s own SHA begins 76c9a79b and its signature status is unsigned.

The commit-pinned detail gives licenseId OGL-UK-2.0, name Open Government Licence v2.0 and isDeprecatedLicenseId false. Both crossRef and seeAlso give http://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/2/. Its text declares version 2.0.

The government capture directly confirms the English UK edition at the cited path, including its declaration at [8250,8300). Its contextual contribution is the identity of the referent. The SPDX detail supplies list membership.

challenge.method: Checked the tag target against the detail URL, compared the UK and Canada v2.0 records and both other UK editions, and compared schemes, edition paths, version declarations and monarch wording.
challenge.results: The SPDX HTTP link and publisher HTTPS capture share the National Archives host and version/2/ path. The v1 navigation link and generic latest link identify alternatives. Canada has a different host, provider and identifier. The recorded crossRef.match is “false”. The publisher names His Majesty’s Stationery Office and the SPDX plain text names Her Majesty’s Stationery Office.

limitations: The unsigned tag documents the repository’s release mapping. The generated record supplies no independent XML build history. Its link supports documentary correspondence only. Work-specific licensing, text equivalence and current registry selection fall outside the claim.
reasoning: The SPDX 3.29.0 target commit contains the generated license detail for OGL-UK-2.0. Its identifier, name, text declaration and two reference fields identify the National Archives edition. Applying SCES §§4 and 7, the shared version number with Canada required a publisher check in addition to the release pin.
